title: Repository access
subtitle: Tokens and keys Studio uses to connect to GitHub, GitLab and other servers.

credentials.title: Tokens and keys
credentials.empty: No access yet. It appears when you connect a repository.
credentials.attention_one: {{count}} token needs attention: the server rejected it or its expiry date has passed or is near.
credentials.attention_other: {{count}} tokens need attention: the server rejected them or their expiry date has passed or is near.

hosts.title: Trusted servers
hosts.empty: No servers yet. A server key is remembered after you confirm it.

secrets.title: Secret storage
secrets.ok: Secrets are stored encrypted in the Studio data folder.
secrets.unavailable: The secret store is unavailable: tokens cannot be saved.
secrets.sharedFolder: The data folder is inside a cloud drive ({{provider}}). Encrypted tokens and the encryption key will end up in the cloud.

secretsUnavailable: The secret store is unavailable: tokens and keys cannot be saved. Check the Studio data folder.

caption.pat: Easiest: Studio shows where to get the token
caption.ssh: One key for all your repositories on the server
caption.deploy: A key for this repository only

mismatch.sshOnHttps: A key works only with an ssh address, but an https address was entered.
mismatch.tokenOnSsh: A token works only with an https address, but an ssh address was entered.

pat.stored: The token is stored encrypted on this computer and is never shown again.
pat.label: Access name
pat.usernameHint: Only needed for servers that ask for a name together with the token. Usually left empty.

ssh.emptyTitle: There is no key for this server yet
ssh.emptyText: Studio will create a key on this computer. The private part stays here, and you add the public part to the repository.
ssh.allowWrite: Do not forget to allow write access for the key (Allow write access): with read-only access versions cannot be sent.
ssh.deployEmptyTitle: There is no deploy key for {{repo}} yet
ssh.deployEmptyText: Studio will create a key on this computer. You add it to this repository only: it gives no access to the others.

scope.deployHint: Access to this repository only. Safer: the key can be revoked without touching anything else.
scope.userHint: One key for all your repositories on this server. Handy when you have several projects.

fix.useBound: Update the access the project is connected with

help.tokenNote: Give the token only the permissions it needs and an expiry date: you can revoke it in the server settings.
help.keyNote: The private part of the key stays on this computer and is never sent anywhere.

token.open: Open Settings, Developer settings, Fine-grained tokens and click Generate new token. The link above has already filled in the name and the Contents right.
token.repo: Under Repository access choose Only select repositories and tick this repository: it cannot be filled in through the link.
token.perm: Under Permissions, Repository permissions Contents must be Read and write.
token.copy: Click Generate token and copy the value: GitHub shows it once.

key.open: Open the repository's Deploy keys page (button below) and click Add deploy key.
key.paste: Paste the public key from the field above, any title.
key.write: Tick Allow write access: without it the repository accepts the key for reading only.

userKey.open: Open Settings, SSH and GPG keys (button below) and click New SSH key.
userKey.paste: Paste the public key from the field above. The key works for all your repositories on GitHub.

token.open: Open Preferences, Access tokens and click Add new token.
token.scope: Check the rights: read_repository and write_repository are needed, without api. The link above has ticked them already.
token.copy: Create the token and copy the value: GitLab shows it once.

key.open: Open the repository's Settings, Repository, Deploy keys and click Add new key.
key.paste: Paste the public key from the field above, any title.
key.write: Turn on Grant write permissions to this key.

userKey.open: Open Preferences, SSH Keys (button below) and click Add new key.
userKey.paste: Paste the public key from the field above. The key works for all your projects on this server.

token.open: Open Settings, Applications and find the access tokens section.
token.perm: Give the token the repository: Read and write permission.
token.copy: Create the token and copy the value: it will not be shown later.

key.open: Open the repository's Settings, Deploy Keys and click Add Deploy Key.
key.paste: Paste the public key from the field above, any title.
key.write: Turn on Enable Write Access: otherwise versions cannot be sent.

userKey.open: Open Settings, SSH / GPG Keys (button below) and click Add Key.
userKey.paste: Paste the public key from the field above. The key works for all your repositories on this server.

token.open: Open Personal settings, App passwords and create an app password.
token.perm: Give it the Repositories: Write permission.
token.copy: Copy the password and paste it here as the token: Bitbucket shows it only once.

key.open: Open the repository's Repository settings, Access keys and click Add key.
key.paste: Paste the public key from the field above, any title.
key.write: Sending versions needs write access: if a Bitbucket repository key is read-only, add the key to your profile under Personal settings, SSH keys.

userKey.open: Open Personal settings, SSH keys (button below) and click Add key.
userKey.paste: Paste the public key from the field above. The key works for all your repositories on Bitbucket.

token.create: Open your profile settings on the server and create a personal access token with write permission for the repository.
token.copy: Copy the value and paste it above: the server usually shows it only once.

key.paste: Add the public key from the field above to the repository settings or your profile on the server.
key.write: Allow the key to write: a read-only key cannot send versions.

userKey.paste: Add the public key from the field above to your profile settings on the server (usually the SSH keys section).

hostKey.unknownText: Studio will remember the server key and recognize it later: this way an impostor server does not get your data. Compare the fingerprint with the one the server publishes and confirm.
hostKey.changedText: The server used to present a different key. The connection is stopped.
hostKey.changedWarning: This may be a server impersonation. If the administrator changed the key on purpose, compare the new fingerprint with the one they published and only then replace the key.
hostKey.typeHost: To replace the key, type the server name: {{host}}
hostKey.whereToCheck: You can compare the fingerprint on the server's page with its ssh keys or with its administrator. If it does not match, decline.
hostKey.failed: Could not remember the server key.
hostKey.revealing: Fetching the fingerprint of the new key…
hostKey.revealFailed: Could not get the new server key fingerprint. The key cannot be replaced blindly.
hostKey.noFingerprint: The new fingerprint is not known yet, the key was not replaced.

credentials.openProject: Open the sync settings of the project “{{name}}”
credentials.authFailedHint: The server did not accept this access. Replace the token or the key.

replaceDialog.title: Replace token
replaceDialog.description: The new token replaces the old one for {{host}}. You can revoke the old token in the server settings.
replaceDialog.keepHint: The token is stored encrypted on this computer and is never shown again.

deleteDialog.title: Delete the access “{{label}}”?
deleteDialog.description: The token or key is erased from the Studio and cannot be restored.
deleteDialog.usedText: Syncing in them stops until you set a new access.
deleteDialog.confirmUsed: Delete and leave the projects without access

hosts.intro: Servers whose keys you confirmed for ssh. If a server key changes, the Studio stops the connection and asks you.
hosts.forgetText: Next time you connect, the Studio shows the key fingerprint again and you have to confirm it.

encryption.title: Encryption
encryption.sourceFile: The encryption key is in a file in the Studio data folder.
encryption.sourceEnv: The encryption key comes from an environment variable and is not in the data folder.
encryption.permissionsOk: The key file is closed to other users of this computer.
encryption.permissionsNotEnforced: The key file is not closed to other users: the system does not let us restrict permissions. Do not give strangers access to the data folder.
encryption.unreadable_one: {{count}} access could not be read: the encryption key was lost or replaced. Enter this token again.
encryption.unreadable_other: {{count}} accesses could not be read: the encryption key was lost or replaced. Enter these tokens again.
encryption.unavailableText: The secret store is unavailable: tokens and keys cannot be saved. Check the Studio data folder and its permissions.
encryption.sharedFolder: The data folder is inside a cloud drive ({{provider}}), so the encrypted tokens and the encryption key go to the cloud together and the encryption protects almost nothing. Move the key file outside the drive: the path is set by the HSE_STUDIO__SECRETS__KEY_FILE variable.
encryption.threat: Encryption protects against accidental leaks: a copy of the data folder, a cloud drive, a screenshot. It does not protect against malware on this computer or against someone who holds the whole data folder together with the key.

fetchDefault.title: Default background check
fetchDefault.text: How often the Studio checks project repositories in the background. You can change it for a single project in its sync settings. This setting is personal and is not shared with colleagues.
fetchDefault.label: Default interval

none.title: Public repository without a token
none.hint: No token or key is needed. If the repository turns out to be private, the check will say so and you can choose a token or a key.
none.cannot: You cannot send your own versions: the project only receives

tokenLink.title: Get a token
tokenLink.prefilled: The name, the description and the needed rights are already filled in through the link.
tokenLink.plain: This page does not accept prefilling: set the rights following the steps below.

create.title: Create
create.text: Open the page and click create token.

copy.title: Copy
copy.text: The server shows the value only once.

paste.title: Paste
paste.text: Paste it in the field below: Studio checks it for you.

tokenLink.githubRepo: On the page choose "Only select repositories" and tick this repository: it cannot be filled in through the link.
tokenLink.gitlabNote: The default lifetime is 365 days, the server administrator may limit it. The api right is not needed and is not requested.

github.lead: Do not need a fine-grained token, or the page did not open?

gitlab.lead: The page did not open? This happens on older GitLab versions.
gitlab.link: Open the page for older versions

gitlabNew.lead: The page did not open? The server may be newer than it looks.
gitlabNew.link: Open the page for newer versions

tokenLink.broad: A classic token gives access to all your repositories. Choose a fine-grained one if you can.
tokenLink.legacyGitlab: This is GitLab {{version}}, an old version: its token page is different. We open the address for older versions.

running.title: Checking the token
running.text: Asking the server whose token this is and what rights it has.

sufficient.title: The token fits
sufficient.text: The rights are enough to read the repository and push versions.

too_narrow.title: The token lacks rights
too_narrow.text: Versions cannot be pushed. Add the rights: {{missing}}. The easiest way is to issue a new token with the link.

too_broad.title: The token has more rights than needed
too_broad.text: Extra rights: {{extra}}. It will work, but it is safer to issue a token for repository read and write only.

unknown.title: Could not check the rights
unknown.text: The server does not show the rights of this token (an older server or a fine-grained token). Writing will be checked when the repository is connected.

expired.title: The token has expired
expired.text: The server will not accept this token any more. Issue a new one and paste it here.

auth_failed.title: The server did not accept the token
auth_failed.text: The token is wrong or revoked. Issue a new one and paste it here.

tls_untrusted_ca.title: The server certificate was issued by an unknown authority
tls_untrusted_ca.text: Add the issuing authority's certificate for this server or pin the certificate fingerprint, then check the token again.

tls_pin_mismatch.title: The server certificate has changed
tls_pin_mismatch.text: It does not match the pinned one. Review it and pin it again if you are sure.

tls_error.title: The server certificate was not accepted
tls_error.text: The certificate could not be verified. For an internal server add the issuing authority's certificate in the server settings.

offline.title: No connection to the server
offline.text: Check your internet and the server address, then retry.

timeout.title: The server did not answer in time

rate_limited.title: Too many requests
rate_limited.text: The server asks you to wait. Check again in a minute.

sso_required.title: The token must be authorized for the organization
sso_required.text: The organization requires SSO. Open the token on the server and authorize it for the organization.

tls.untrustedTitle: The certificate of {{host}} is not from a known authority
tls.untrustedText: A server inside an organization is often signed by its own authority. Studio never turns the check off: you either add the authority's certificate or pin this server's certificate.
tls.mismatchText: You pinned a different certificate for this server earlier.
tls.mismatchWarning: If the administrator did not renew or replace the certificate, this may be a substitution. Do not pin the new fingerprint before you find out.

ca.text: You need the certificate of your organization's issuing authority (root or intermediate). The server administrator provides it. A private key is not needed and not accepted.

drop.title: Drop the certificate file here or

ca.stored: The certificate is stored on this computer next to the tokens and works only for {{host}}.

problem.private_key: This is a private key. It must not be sent anywhere. Only the certificate is needed: the BEGIN CERTIFICATE block.
problem.not_pem: This does not look like a certificate. The text between BEGIN CERTIFICATE and END CERTIFICATE is needed.
problem.too_large: The file is too large for a certificate.

pin.text: Studio will remember the fingerprint of this server's certificate and recognize it later, like a server key in ssh. Compare the fingerprint with the server administrator.
pin.confirm: I compared the fingerprint with the server administrator or another reliable source
pin.typeHost: To pin the new certificate, type the server name: {{host}}
pin.noCertificate: The server did not send a certificate. Check again to see it.

tls.noDisable: The certificate check cannot be turned off: Studio does not send tokens to a server it does not trust.
tls.failed: Could not save the server settings.

servers.title: Git servers
servers.intro: Server type, your own issuing authority certificate and a pinned certificate. Needed for GitLab and other servers inside an organization.
servers.empty: No servers yet. They appear when you connect a repository, or add a server in advance.

detectedBy.api: Type detected from the server's answer

servers.saveFailed: Could not save the server settings.
servers.removeFailed: Could not remove the server settings.

dialog.description: The settings apply to all projects and accesses of this server.
dialog.hostInvalid: A server name is needed, for example gitlab.hse.local.
dialog.caWillGo: The certificate is removed on save. You can paste a new one below.
dialog.pinWillGo: The pin is removed on save.
